analysis.title: Global oil market tracker, Issue 25: 16 November 2026
key_insights: ANZ rates its Oil Market Resilience Dashboard red overall. Logistics are under stress, while supply, inventories, refining and effective spare capacity are rated vulnerable.

Four-week average Persian Gulf crude exports fell to 12.5mb/d. Ship tracking suggests the decline accelerated after 13 November and was centred on the UAE. Product exports, particularly distillates, remain heavily constrained.
Effective throughput through the Strait of Hormuz is 49% of the pre-conflict norm, down from 56% the prior week. ANZ calls the Strait the market's binding constraint.

Recorded Hormuz transits edged up, with outbound journeys improving marginally and inbound near zero. Dark-fleet traffic fell to a seven-day average of one vessel per day from 2.1 last week and 2.4 at the start of November.
Alternative export routes are stretched. Saudi Yanbu loadings stayed depressed because Saudi Arabia favours Ras Tanura, and Houthi threats to Red Sea energy infrastructure continue.
Surplus OPEC capacity is 0mb/d under prevailing conditions. ANZ says another hit to shipping or export infrastructure would produce a larger and more persistent supply shock.
Global distillate inventories are 6.1% below the five-year average and global product stocks outside China declined. Crude inventories had small gains in most regions.
Diesel cracks rebounded to USD88.8/bbl as Russian and Middle East supply stays constrained. Russian diesel exports slumped at the start of November after Ukrainian attacks on refineries.
Crude futures recovered as expectations of a near-term peace deal and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz diminished. Oil product prices edged higher.

Dated Brent's premium to front-month futures stayed near zero, driven by weaker spot prices on hopes of an end to the conflict. Longer-dated futures were stable, which ANZ reads as an unchanged medium-term view.

ANZ's Oil Market Fundamental Expectations Index moved out of the extremely tight range to balanced (0 to 0.5) in November, mostly because the spread between 1st and 22nd month Brent futures contracted.
Investors marginally cut bullish Brent bets after three weekly gains, and trimmed WTI net longs slightly.
US crude output was broadly stable, while US crude and distillate exports declined further. The US SPR drawdown rate rose to 2.65mbbl and reserves fell below 279.5mbbl, the lowest since 1982.
Australian diesel cover rose to 31 days and Singapore fuel inventories rose across all products. Refinery run rates were broadly higher in China and the US.

sector_views.rationale: Not a rating. ANZ describes physical tightness in crude logistics and diesel with no spare capacity cushion, so prices are highly sensitive to another supply shock.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Deliverable supply is exposed to further disruption, with the decline accelerating after 13 November.
Down from 56% the prior week. Logistics is the binding constraint on supply.

macro_indicators.indicator: Global distillate inventories vs five-year average
macro_indicators.interpretation: Diesel is the main downstream pressure point.
Refining margins rebounded as physical markets stay tight.
No effective supply buffer under prevailing conditions, so prices are sensitive to any new physical shock.
Lowest level since 1982, with the drawdown flow rate at 2.65mbbl.
Moved out of the extremely tight range, mostly on the contraction of the 1st to 22nd month Brent spread.

risk_factors: Renewed attacks or operating setbacks at Persian Gulf energy infrastructure, including Houthi threats near the Red Sea.
Another hit to shipping or export infrastructure would produce a larger and more persistent supply shock because of tight tanker availability, depleted inventories and zero spare OPEC capacity.
Further falls in Hormuz throughput and Persian Gulf exports, particularly from the UAE.
Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries are cutting Russian diesel exports, which tightens distillates.
A peace deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz would add supply and is the main downside risk to the tight physical picture.
charts_described: Oil Market Resilience Dashboard rates Persian Gulf exports 12.5mb/d, Hormuz throughput 49% of normal, distillate inventories -6.1% vs 5y avg, diesel cracks USD88.8/bbl and surplus OPEC capacity 0mb/d, with an overall assessment of Vulnerable.
Singapore fuel inventories rose across all products and Australian fuel stocks recorded strong gains, per the captions.
vol_and_positioning: Investors marginally reduced bullish Brent bets, with net longs declining after three consecutive weekly gains.
WTI positioning is cautious, with a slight decline in net long positions.
Dated Brent's premium to the front-month future stayed near zero, and longer-dated futures were stable.
geopolitical: Houthis claimed attacks last week on a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the path to ending the conflict is open if the US accepts Iran's logical conditions. ANZ says to watch the US response.
Ukraine ramped up attacks on Russian energy infrastructure and ANZ sees escalation of the Russia-Ukraine conflict as a distinct possibility.
Expectations of a near-term peace deal and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz diminished last week.
Dark-fleet and recorded tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains minimal.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical markets stay tight. Hormuz throughput is 49% of normal, distillate stocks are 6.1% below average, diesel cracks rebounded to USD88.8/bbl and spare OPEC capacity is 0mb/d, so prices are highly sensitive to another shock.
tension_points.bear_case: Hopes of a peace deal and reopening of the Strait could add supply. Dated Brent's premium fell to near zero on weaker spot prices, and the OMFEI contracted to balanced as the 1st to 22nd month Brent spread narrowed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A peace deal that reopens the Strait of Hormuz and lifts Persian Gulf exports above 12.5mb/d.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Strait of Hormuz is the binding constraint, and with no spare capacity another hit to shipping or exports would cause a larger, more persistent supply shock.
theme_stances.evidence: The Strait of Hormuz has become the market's binding constraint.

theme_stances.evidence: Diesel is the main downstream pressure point.
